summary.one_liner: A regression suite of TLA+ security models for Clawdbot, checked with the TLC model checker, where "green" models should pass and deliberately buggy "red" models should produce counterexample traces.
summary.what_it_does: The repo holds TLA+ specifications under tla/specs and TLC model configs under tla/models, with a make target to run a chosen model. Green models are expected to pass with no invariant violation, while red models are intentionally buggy variants that should fail and emit a counterexample trace. A docs folder covers how to interpret results, a claim inventory, and a verification roadmap. It also includes a conformance step: a script (scripts/extract-tool-groups.mjs) reads tool-group expansions and tool-name aliases from the Clawdbot main repo's tool-policy.ts and writes generated/tool-groups.json. The README says CI currently runs TLC targets directly, and a planned mode would check that generated artifacts do not drift from the main repo.
use_cases: Model-checking security properties of Clawdbot agent tool policies
Running TLC regression checks on TLA+ security specs
Verifying that formal models match Clawdbot's tool-group constants
Demonstrating security bugs via counterexample traces
Reviewing documented security claims and verification roadmap
how_to_run: make <target>  (run a specific TLC target; see docs/formal-models.md for the recommended run set)
node scripts/extract-tool-groups.mjs  (regenerate generated/tool-groups.json; expects the Clawdbot repo checked out at ../clawdbot)
notable: Green/red model pairing: red variants are deliberately buggy and should produce counterexample traces
Conformance checks extract tool-group and alias constants from the Clawdbot TypeScript source
Pinned tla2tools.jar shipped in tools/tla for reproducible runs
Structured as a security regression suite rather than a one-off proof
caveats: Requires Java and a local TLC setup; the conformance script expects a sibling clawdbot checkout at ../clawdbot
Conformance drift checking in CI is described as planned, not yet implemented
README lists open fidelity gaps: pairing-store concurrency/locking, provider-specific ingress nuances, routing identity-link semantics
